subject: EU-West: planned driver & kernel rollout — impact window (May 20-21)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Horizon Financial <ops@horizonfin.com>, Dovetail Analytics <infra@dovetail.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T08:00:00Z
Subject: EU-West: planned driver & kernel rollout — impact window (May 20-21)

Hi all,

Heads up: we’re scheduling a planned maintenance to roll a tested GPU driver + kernel compatibility update across our eu-west host pool. Window: Tue May 20 22:00 UTC → Wed May 21 04:00 UTC. This is a staged, rolling restart across availability groups; we expect staggered restarts per host with automatic traffic migration.

What to expect:
- Scope: kernel modules + NVIDIA driver micro-update. No model weight changes.
- Impact: short reconnections for in-flight sessions during the node restart (typically <30s); a small number of requests may see increased tail latency as sessions reconnect.
- Canary/rollback: we will run canaries on ~2% of capacity for 2 hours before ramping; automated rollback available if error rates exceed thresholds.
- SLOs: we aim to remain within standard latency targets; we will trigger fallbacks to a compatible model variant if any degradation persists.

Attachments: drivers_release_notes_v2.pdf (notes)
Link: https://status.redwood.com/maintenance/2025-05-eu-west-driver-rollout

Action requested from Horizon Financial: please confirm whether you want us to (A) apply the change to all production traffic during the window, or (B) exclude a labeled tenant pool so you can validate on your own schedule. If no response by Tue May 13 17:00 UTC we will proceed with default rolling application.

If you have any strict blackout periods within the window, reply with exact times and we’ll do our best to accommodate.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ops Team <ops@horizonfin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-West: planned driver & kernel rollout — impact window (May 20-21)

Thanks, Jordan. Quick questions: 1) Will active KV cache sessions persist through a node failover or will they need warm-up? 2) Any expected change to affinity for reserved endpoints (we use pinned model instances for trading pipelines)?

If rollback is available, we prefer you keep our traffic in the standard pool so your canaries cover our traffic unless there's a risk of extended reconnection time.

— Mike (Horizon ops)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Horizon Financial <ops@horizonfin.com>, Dovetail Analytics <infra@dovetail.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-12T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-West: planned driver & kernel rollout — impact window (May 20-21)

Hi Mike — thanks for the precision. Short answers:

1) KV cache: prefix and session KV are preserved when we migrate live sessions; there will be a short period where the client reconnects to a new backend and rehydrates local caches. For our streaming API sessions, the majority of calls will continue; you may see a single reconnect event. Warm-up is recommended for ultra-low-latency trading workloads — consider a brief synthetic traffic run after the canary completes.

2) Reserved/pinned instances: our scheduled driver roll will respect pinned assignments for dedicated capacity. For shared-host customers (default), affinity is best-effort during restarts but cannot be strictly guaranteed. If Horizon is using reserved endpoints, there should be no affinity change. Please confirm whether you’re on a reserved tenant.

Operational mitigations we’ll run:
- 2% canary for 2 hours, then staged ramp to 25% → 60% → 100% over 6 hours.
- Active health checks and immediate rollback if 5xx or tail latency > 3x baseline for the canary window.
- Staggered host restarts to maintain capacity; control-plane will drain connections prior to reboot.

Attachments: canary_rollout_plan.csv
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XxExampleInternalDocLink

If you want us to exclude a label, reply with the label id and we’ll honor it. Otherwise we’ll include Horizon traffic in the canary by default per Jordan's note.

Marissa
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-13T09:00:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-West: planned driver & kernel rollout — impact window (May 20-21)

Team — Horizon confirmed they want to be included in the canary (no reserved endpoint). Please ensure runbook and Pager duty rotation are set. Karthik: can you publish the on-call runbook and post a brief note to #ops-announce with the exact host group names and expected restart sequence? Grace: coordinate with Platform to hold a 30-minute monitoring watch starting at 21:30 UTC on May 20.

We’ll escalate to execs if rollback is triggered and the impact extends beyond 30 minutes for affected tenants. Attaching runbook_oncall_checklist.txt for checklist items.

Thanks — Jordan
